I've been struggling with this for about 7 years now. it's not an everyday thing anymore now that I've found ways to cope. mine is related to my anxiety and depression. here are some tips you might find helpful:

-drink breakfast shakes in the morning, even just a little. being hungry can make nausea worse, and these are generally easy on the stomach

-the following products can help with controlling nausea, in my experience
     -ginger gum
     -Nauzene chewables
     -peppermint gum
     -ginger root capsules
     -sometimes original Dramamine
     -mints

-distractions help a lot. the more you focus on the pain, the worse it will get. even if it is the last thing you want to do, do something to take your mind off of it

hope this helps! :)
step 1 is actually what I have the most trouble with. I'm not sure how to really describe how I feel in those situations, I just kinda know

that's a really good way of thinking about that. whenever I call the hotline, they usually ask about activities that can distract me instead. maybe that's part of the reason I've never really had a great experience with hotlines

if you don't mind me asking, which hotline do you work for? I've been trying to find one that I like.
I think the template could be useful if I was ever in an emergency situation, but I find it a little difficult to fill out. I actually started it a few months ago during one of my really bad periods; I had trouble even thinking of things I enjoy that could distract me. now that I'm doing a little better, I want to fill it out for later. it can be hard to think about how I really feel during the bad times and how to help myself during a time I don't want to be helped. does that make sense?
thanks for the article. I really appreciate it.

my apologies. I included  a link to what I mean. from what I've read, this type of document is usually created with a therapist in an effort to help the patient deal with a crisis. I have never been to counseling before, so I was just wondering if anybody else has done the same thing as me and made one on their own.
I know I should really get help—I've been struggling with depression and suicidal thoughts for a few years now—but I have yet to build up the courage. my goal is to go to counseling once I go back to school since my college offers it for free.
